newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria budget deficit up to 198 bln levs Feb 17.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria budget deficit up to 198 bln levs Feb 17.

text.p: Bulgaria's central government budget deficit rose by 32.4 billion levs ($15.3 million) in the first half of February to 197.8 billion levs, preliminary Finance Ministry figures showed.
BULGARIA BUDGET DEFICIT, bln levs FEB 17 JAN 31
"The increase was a result of large interest payments on government securities and on direct loans from financial institutions," a Finance Ministry official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.
The ministry paid a total of 39.144 billion levs interest on treasury paper and on loans from the Bulgarian National Bank, the State Savings Banks and commercial banks in the first half of February.
The high central interst rate (CIR) of 16.50 percent monthly and new short-term T-bill issues have put a heavy burden on the budget, the official added.
The Finance Ministry has issued one- and four-week discount T-bill issues daily since January 20 to regulate excessive banks' liquidity.
Bulgaria's parliament approved on January 31 a stop-gap budget bill to service large government debt payments and finance public spending until a viable 1997 budget is passed.
The deficit assumed in the bill was limited to the amount of interest payments due on government debt.

The bill provided for a 100-percent increase in public employees' salaries, pensions and social benefits. Under the bill, state debt would be refinanced through new government securities issues and a direct 20-year loan from the central bank. The amount of the credit was not specified. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569; 981 4145 ($ = 2120 Bulgarian Levs)
